reader.requirement: At --std 85 the arguments of a function reference are evaluated one by one, left to right in list order; an argument may itself be a function-identifier or an arithmetic expression containing one, including a reference to the same function; at 85 the order is observable only through RANDOM's seed state (no user-defined functions or object properties exist), and the witness exercises exactly that plus nesting.
reader.edition-search: grep of Edition/DialectLevel/ConstructRegistry/DialectBehavior over Binding/Procedure/ArgumentOrder.cs: no hit; IntrinsicBinder's edition consults (COBOL1502 window, SR4 placement, integer-date bound, ArgPredicate.AppliesAt) gate WHICH functions/arguments bind, not their evaluation order. The order is one edition-independent mechanism (ArgumentOrder windows, the bound argument list rendered in order).

reader.notes: ArgumentOrder (one mechanism for every function reference) keeps each argument at its list position and materializes an earlier argument only when a later one registers pre-ops; at 85 no argument registers pre-ops (no user functions, properties or function subscripts, the last refused by COBOL0900), so the bound list renders in order. The RANDOM probes and the witness's ORDER line show left-to-right consumption of the seed sequence.

refuter.evidence: Probe g2-001 at --std 85: four RANDOM draws from seed 5 stored one per statement give XE=+0654.854662857523 for s1+10*s2+100*s3+1000*s4; the same draws consumed by FUNCTION SUM (RANDOM(5)*1, SUM(RANDOM*10, RANDOM*100), RANDOM*1000), a nested argument list, give XA=+0654.854662858347 (difference 8e-10 from storing each s in V9(12); any other order would differ by hundreds), so arguments, including those of a nested function, are evaluated left to right. ALL-subscript order (the 1989 module's 2.2, which fixes the argument list's order): ORD-MAX(TC(ALL ALL)) on a 2x3 table with the maximum at (1,2) gives 2 and at (2,1) gives 4 (rightmost subscript varies fastest); ORD-MIN(TC(2 ALL)) gives 2; ORD-MIN(TV(ALL) 5) with ODO N=2 gives 2 (only the current occurrences, then the literal). The reader's FACTORIAL(FACTORIAL(3)) covers the same-function sentence. cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.4 GR2 'its arguments are evaluated individually in the order specified in the list of arguments'; --find located §1989:p.A-28 'the effect is as if each table element associated with that subscript position were specified'. No edition consult on the order path beyond those the reader listed.
